**GENERATED FILE — do not edit.** Regenerate with:
`python3 scripts/factory-knowledge/generate_current.py`

One line per decision still in force, newest first. The full record — evidence,
scope, what it replaced — is the file named by the ID in `decisions/`.

tool-managed machine format — nobody should ever be sent to read one raw.

**122 current · 8 superseded**

- **DEC-20260903-008** (2026-09-03, procurement) — THE STORE ROLE HOLDS FULL PROCUREMENT WRITE, SO A STOREKEEPER MAY APPROVE A PURCHASE REQUISITION. Store already held procurement.view on the live instance and could see procurement but not act in it; approval is gated on the procurement WRITE permission, so the store user was refused. The whole change is one permission, procurement.manage, ADDED to the role - never syncing or rewriting the five other permissions an administrator granted Store through the Roles screen. THE TRADE-OFF, NAMED: the procurement module has ONE write permission covering requisitions and their approval, purchase orders, goods receipts and vendors; there is no narrower approve-only grant, so this also lets Store raise requisitions and purchase orders and record goods receipts - the same trade-off the owner accepted for Accounts in DEC-20260903-006. FC-06 IS INTACT AND HAS ONE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE. The purchase rate is Owner/Accounts only, and the gate ships: PurchaseOrderLineResource and GoodsReceiptNoteLineResource OMIT unit_price for a reader without finance.view or finance.manage, and supplier bills sit behind the finance module entirely, so Store cannot READ a purchase rate. But creating and amending a purchase order both REQUIRE unit_price, so a Store user cannot amend a purchase order without typing a rate they cannot see, which would overwrite the real one. PURCHASE ORDERS THEREFORE STAY WITH ACCOUNTS AND THE OWNER IN PRACTICE; what this grant is for is requisition approval and goods receipts. Nobody is assigned to any role by this change - who keeps the store stays a person's decision on the Roles screen.
  - evidence: Owner messages from Muthukumar Panchabekasan, 03-Sep-2026, in Claude Code session https://claude.ai/code/session_01SvgeRzjAyQuucri74QU27R. First, on being shown a live screenshot of the store user unable to approve: 'store stil unabe to approve' and 'yes, full procurement for Accounts, record and build it' (recorded as DEC-20260903-006, which granted Accounts). Then, told that the Store role still lacked the procurement write permission on the live Roles screen, the owner instructed: 'give store the procurement rights'. The live permission board was read first with the read-only roles:show workflow (run 33775271312, 03-Sep-2026): Store users=1 permissions consumption-substitute.view, inventory.view, maintenance.view, procurement.view, production.view, users.view.
- **DEC-20260903-007** (2026-09-03, production, quality) — A BATCH THAT HAS BEEN HANDED OVER MAY STILL BE RETURNED BY QUALITY AND CORRECTED BY THE SUPERVISOR; ONLY A CHANGE TO THE CLOSING COUNT THE NEXT SHIFT OPENED FROM IS REFUSED. The floor's flow is: start the batch, complete it, and it stands in the shift floor queue with its status; corrections are possible while it waits; Quality either records its check and the batch goes on to the Plant Manager and Accounts, or Quality sends it back; a batch sent back is corrected IN THE SHIFT FLOOR QUEUE. Nothing is ever sent back to a machine and no run is repeated - the machine has moved on and only the paperwork is wrong. Until now the ERP refused every correction to a segment that had handed over to a following one, on the ground that the following segment opens from this one's closing figures. That guard is WIDER THAN ITS OWN REASON: what a following segment inherits is exactly ONE number, the counted closing bin weight in kilograms, recorded as its own count movement - not the pieces produced, not the rejects, not the reason. So a batch with a following segment may be returned and corrected, and the refusal fires ONLY where the correction would change that closing count while a following segment stands on it; the refusal names that reason. THE SUPERVISOR may make the correction, not only the Plant Manager. EXPRESSLY NOT BUILT: correcting a chain - reopening the following segment and restating its opening - because that rewrites a shift somebody has already signed; where a correction genuinely needs the closing count changed, the ERP refuses today and the factory decides later whether a chain correction should exist. Every other correction gate stands unchanged: an approved, synced, failed or rejected batch, or one already on a Tally voucher, is still refused.
  - evidence: Owner messages from Muthukumar Panchabekasan, 03-Sep-2026, in Claude Code session https://claude.ai/code/session_01SvgeRzjAyQuucri74QU27R, after Quality was refused a return on batch 20260902-M03-002 with reason 'qty mismatch'. The owner described the intended flow verbatim: 'the flow shoud be like this start batch and end then it will be in shift fllor queue with current stauts , quality approve it move to proaudion the entry will be availabel in the shfit floor pagetoo and approver page, here before the quality approve we can do some correction if the qualith send back it shoud be edit option in shfit follor queue, how you expect send it back to the machine itself ?'. Shown that a following segment inherits only the counted closing bin weight (DayBinLedgerService::openingFor reading closingFor, a recorded count movement) and asked who may edit and what should happen when the closing weight itself must change, the owner answered verbatim: 'supervisor can edit, refuse if closing weight changes'.

- **DEC-20260903-005** (2026-09-03, hrms, payroll) — A day of attendance is judged by the HOURS WORKED against the eight-hour factory shift, not by the Full Day or Half Day label printed by the Pooja punch app. Eight hours is a full day and four hours is a half day. The app label cannot be trusted: in the July 2026 report 245 days were marked Half Day and 232 of those had seven hours or more worked, because the app measures every shift against a longer general day, so real eight-hour shifts that clocked out a few minutes early were recorded as halves. Applying that month as printed would have paid 232 full shifts as halves, about 116 days of pay across 59 people in one month. The factory runs three shifts, roughly 06:00 to 14:00, 14:00 to 22:00 and 22:00 to 06:00, plus a 09:00 to 18:00 office day, which is why one yardstick cannot judge them all.
  - evidence: Owner message 03-Sep-2026 answering the July punch-report analysis: 8 hour shift is full day, 4 hours half day. Evidence: Employee-day-wise-master-report 2026-07-01 to 2026-07-31, 1829 employee-days, 245 marked HD of which 232 worked 7h or more, three shift patterns visible in the punch pairs.
- **DEC-20260903-004** (2026-09-03, sales, finance, tally-sync) — THE ERP'S OWN SALES INVOICE IS RETIRED; THE IMPORTED TALLY SALES INVOICE, MATCHED TO THE ORDER, IS THE ERP'S INVOICE RECORD. Tally originates the sales invoice, the e-invoice and the IRN (DEC-20260831-012) and the ERP imports and matches it to a confirmed order (DEC-20260902-046), so the ERP raises no invoice document of its own: the Invoices screen and the routes that create or issue an ERP invoice are withdrawn, and no proforma document replaces them (quotations are out of scope, DEC-20260902-052). Existing ERP invoice rows stay as read-only history, never edited or deleted, and an order's trace may still show them as history. Figures the ERP currently builds on its own invoices - receivables, GST returns - are no longer built on the retired document; where they read from instead is answered by the Tally invoice import build (DEC-20260902-046), not by this record. Until the routes are withdrawn, an ERP invoice can never bill more than the customer ordered (PR #88). Resolves Q96.

- **DEC-20260902-042** (2026-09-02, quality, inventory, sales, production) — COMPLETED FINISHED GOODS ARE QUALITY-PENDING UNTIL THE BATCH'S QUALITY CHECK RECORDS THEM; ONLY THE OK QUANTITY BECOMES AVAILABLE AND HOLDABLE. Finished goods received into the Store at Complete Batch (DEC-20260902-016) may be visible in the Store as Quality Pending, but they must not be available for holding, dispatch approval or delivery until the batch's Quality stage (DEC-20260902-006) records the OK and rejected counts. After that, only the OK quantity becomes available and holdable; the rejected quantity follows the scrap process (FC-02, DEC-20260805-001). A hold can therefore only ever cover checked goods, and Internal Quality's line-level dispatch approval (DEC-20260831-006, DEC-20260902-041) is unchanged. This is enforced ON THE SERVER for both the carton-scan and the typed delivery paths: a hold, an approval or a delivery that would draw on Quality-pending goods is refused, never merely hidden. The mechanism is the same by-construction one incoming QA and the damaged-return hold already use - a stock state the Store cannot issue from (DEC-20260825-001, DEC-20260901-003) - and the Store dashboard's completed, Quality-pending, approved and rejected figures (DEC-20260902-016) read from it. ROLLOUT, part of the rule: before this is switched on, a READ-ONLY count of the existing live Quality-pending finished goods is taken on the live instance and reviewed by a person; nothing is assumed and no stock is moved by the rollout. Expressly NOT decided here: which internal location or state name carries the Quality-pending goods, an engineering choice, and what happens to any live goods found pending at rollout, which the count informs and a person decides.

Completed finished goods may be visible in Store as Quality Pending, but they must not be available for holding, dispatch approval or delivery. After batch Quality records the OK and rejected counts, only the OK quantity becomes available and holdable. Rejected quantity follows the scrap process. Enforce this on the server for carton scans and typed delivery paths. Before rollout, perform a read-only count of existing live Quality-pending finished goods.' Quoted in docs/factory/workflows/03-SALES-AND-DISPATCH.md.
- **DEC-20260902-041** (2026-09-02, sales, quality, inventory) — QUALITY APPROVES A SALES ORDER LINE ONLY AFTER ITS FULL QUANTITY IS HELD; THE STORE MAY THEN DISPATCH THE APPROVED QUANTITY IN PARTS, AND THE APPROVAL CANNOT BE WITHDRAWN ONCE ANY OF IT HAS GONE. Internal Quality records dispatch approval for a line only when the full line quantity is held (DEC-20260831-006 unchanged). After that approval the Store (DEC-20260901-005) may dispatch the approved quantity in one or more partial deliveries: each dispatch reduces ERP stock only by the quantity actually dispatched; the line remains partly dispatched until the whole approved quantity has gone; the total dispatched must never exceed the approved quantity, and the Store can never dispatch more than the remaining approved quantity. After the first dispatch the Quality approval cannot be withdrawn, and the remaining approved quantity may be dispatched later under the same approval. Sales is never required to split a line to dispatch in parts, and no truck needs a fresh Quality approval. This is a DECLARED clarification of DEC-20260831-006: it closes that record's expressly open clause on whether Quality may withdraw an approval after goods have moved (no, once any quantity has been dispatched), and states the partial-dispatch reading of 'a line may not be dispatched beyond the quantity Quality approved'. Whether an approval may be withdrawn BEFORE any dispatch is not decided here.

- **DEC-20260902-036** (2026-09-02, inventory, production, quality) — A DAMAGED PET RESIN BAG MAY GO TO QUALITY HOLD ONLY WHEN IT HAS NOT BEEN TIPPED INTO THE BIN AND REMAINS PHYSICALLY IDENTIFIABLE BY ITS BARCODE. Quality then either confirms damage to scrap or releases the material through the existing Quality path (DEC-20260901-003). Resin already tipped into the bin, and any material with no identifiable container or barcode, cannot use this path. The scan of a damaged bag at the return is a return scan, not a load scan, and is the one exception to the no-second-scan rule of DEC-20260902-002. - **DEC-20260902-027** (2026-09-02, inventory, products) — THE PRODUCTION-INPUT FLAG REMAINS THE ONLY ELIGIBILITY RULE FOR STORE MATERIAL REQUESTS AND STORE ISSUES; CATEGORY IS INFORMATIONAL. An active item is requestable only when an authorised person has marked it as a production input, regardless of its current category. Category must not automatically enable or refuse an item on a material request or a Store Issue. If the flag conflicts with the category - for example a finished good marked as a production input - the screen shows a clear warning so the master data can be reviewed, but the flag is never changed silently. It does NOT show supplier identity or purchase rate to Quality: FC-06 stands as written, and the PO and GRN references provide enough traceability without them. The inspected quantity IS the full received quantity and is never typed again; accepted plus rejected must equal received. The checklist changes nothing in stock: the accepted and rejected quantities remain the only stock action, and no second stock path is created. For counted packaging materials the bag and weight fields are hidden until Q87 defines how a counted arrival is recorded. EXPRESSLY NOT DECIDED HERE: whether QC may split one bag's kilograms, what Tally receives for a rejection, and any tolerance or verdict on the sample weight.

- **DEC-20260902-003** (2026-09-02, inventory, production) — MATERIAL THAT GOES INTO THE COMMON DAY BIN IS NEVER RETURNED TO THE STORE; EVERY OTHER MATERIAL MAY BE SENT BACK AT THE END OF THE DAY. The rule is by FLOW, not by item name: once material has been tipped into the centralised day bin - PET resin is the case the owner named first, and anything else that goes into the bin is treated the same - it is not returned, not partially, not fully, not at the end of the day; it stays on the floor and is consumed from there. Material that is still in its bag, box or roll - packing material, and any other input that does not go into the bin - may be sent back at the end of the day, partially or fully, exactly as DEC-20260831-005 and DEC-20260901-001 provide. This NARROWS those two decisions to non-bin materials and changes nothing else in them: a return still names the Store Issue that put the material there (DEC-20260831-008), a full return is still not mandatory, material not returned still remains in Production/WIP as the next day's opening material, and the next request is still netted against the usable Production/WIP quantity for the same item and unit - bin materials included, since they stay on the floor. A damaged return of a returnable material still goes to quality inspection (DEC-20260901-003). Consequence for the ERP: the return screen must refuse a bin-material line with a plain message, never hide it and never accept it. EXPRESSLY NOT DECIDED HERE: how the ERP knows which items go into the day bin once the floor no longer scans at load (DEC-20260902-002) - today that fact is carried only by the act of scanning a bag at the bin, and no item flag records it; this is added to PENDING Q94 as clause (c). Whether masterbatch goes into the bin is a fact about the floor that no primary source states, and it is not decided here.

- **DEC-20260901-007** (2026-09-01, production, inventory) — Recording a production consumption line the run was NOT PLANNED ON requires consumption-substitute.manage, and that permission is held by ADMINISTRATOR AND PLANT MANAGER, and by nobody else by default. This resolves PENDING Q91. Accounts is deliberately NOT granted: booking what a machine ate is a floor act, not a books one. The SUPERVISOR role does not hold it, so the reason box alone is not the control - the completion drawer refuses the line and tells the supervisor to fetch an authorised person, and the Plant Manager is that person because they are on the floor when a material runs out. The second lever the question named - widening what counts as PLANNED in RunConsumableOptionsService::expectedItemIds() - was expressly NOT pulled: incomplete BOMs, packing mappings and dosing rows are the real reason an ordinary line reads as unplanned, and widening the planned set would hide that rather than fix it. The grant is made with givePermissionTo and never syncPermissions, following the carton-trace precedent, so the seeder re-running on every deploy only ever ADDS this one permission and never rewrites what an administrator configured through the Roles screen. SEPARATELY AND IN THE SAME BREATH, the added line now satisfies DEC-20260901-004 in full: it carries substitutes_item_id, the item it stood in for, beside the reason and the author it already carried. That column is NULLABLE and is not required on every added line, because an added line is not always a substitution - a run may book a consumable that replaced nothing, and forcing a name there would make somebody invent a factory value. Every added line still requires its reason; a line that IS a substitution also names what it replaced, and it does so with the same column and the same predicate store_issue_lines uses, so the storekeeper's handover and the machine's actual consumption answer the question identically. This is a WHO-MAY-RECORD rule and remains expressly NOT the approver-above-the-recorder that DEC-20260901-004 leaves undecided and unbuilt; no approval workflow exists.

Port the required missing items from PR #73: the substitutes_item_id linkage required by DEC-20260901-004, the DependencyCheck declaration, the incoming-QC hold filter, and the correctly renumbered pending voucher question.' The same instruction directed that claude/production-consumption-list be the base and that PR #73 be CLOSED rather than merged, so there is one production implementation rather than two. - **DEC-20260901-006** (2026-09-01, production, quality, inventory) — THE DAMAGED FINISHED GOOD REACHES SCRAP THE SAME WAY DAMAGED RETURNED MATERIAL DOES: through Quality, never straight out of stock. DEC-20260901-002 settled that a damaged finished good BECOMES SCRAP but expressly did not authorise building the path, leaving it as a separate deliberate piece of work; the owner has now asked for that path, so this decision authorises it and nothing wider. THE FLOW. The Store reports a finished good as damaged; the quantity moves OUT OF THE FINISHED-GOODS STORE and INTO THE QUALITY-HOLD LOCATION, so it is out of issuable, sellable and dispatchable stock from the moment it is reported, by construction rather than by a filter. Quality then does exactly what it already does for returned material: CONFIRM DAMAGE, which scraps the quantity, or RELEASE it back to a store when it looks and the goods are fine. Reporting is not scrapping and the Store cannot scrap on its own - only Quality's confirmation takes the quantity out of stock, which is the whole meaning of 'to Quality first'. IT REUSES THE SIBLING PATH RATHER THAN COPYING IT. The quality-hold location (DEC-20260901-003), the standing-in-hold read, confirm-damage and release are the SAME code that already serves damaged returned material; those operate on an item and a location and never cared which kind of item it was. Only the DOOR IN is new, because until now the only way into quality hold was material coming back off the floor. Two behaviours a copy would have drifted on are therefore free: a hold is bounded by what is actually standing, and dispositions move in item order so two of them cannot deadlock. WHICH SCRAP ITEM IS STILL NOT DECIDED, and this decision does not need it. Scrap is an ISSUE OUT OF STOCK carrying purpose 'scrap', not a change of item identity and not an inward booking against a Scrap master - the same route incoming QC uses for material it rejects. DEC-20260901-002's third boundary therefore stands untouched: no scrap item is named, and no Tally master is invented. NOTHING IS POSTED TO TALLY. What Tally should receive when a finished good is scrapped is undecided, exactly as it is for scrapped returned material (DEC-20260901-003) and for QA rejection at arrival (DEC-20260825-001). The stock fact is recorded and the voucher waits for the answer. THE DOOR IS FINISHED GOODS ONLY. A line naming an item that is not a finished good is refused and pointed at the returned-material door, so the two paths cannot be used interchangeably and DEC-20260901-002's finished-goods answer is not quietly read across onto raw or packing material, whose disposition DEC-20260901-003 settles separately. EXPRESSLY NOT DECIDED: whether a damaged finished good already promised to a customer should release its reservation when reported, and whether a dispatched carton found damaged AFTER it left may come back through this door - both are returns from a customer, which this factory has no path for at all.
  - evidence: Owner instruction 01-Sep-2026: 'Finish the remaining Production workflow and damaged finished goods to Quality to Scrap flow', together with the 01-Sep decision list 'Damaged finished goods go to Scrap' and 'Damaged returned material goes to Quality first. After Quality confirms damage, move it to Scrap.' Lifts boundary (2) of DEC-20260901-002 ('Nothing here authorises building a finished-good-to-scrap conversion flow'); boundary (3), which Scrap item, is left standing and is not needed because scrap is an issue out of stock.
- **DEC-20260901-005** (2026-09-01, sales, inventory, quality) — THE STORE performs the final dispatch action, and SALES does not. This resolves Q78, which DEC-20260831-006 left expressly open ('whether the Store, rather than Sales, performs the final dispatch act'). The sequence DEC-20260831-006 fixed is otherwise unchanged and every gate in it stands: stock is held in full against the sales order line, then internal Quality approves and that approval is RECORDED against the line (who, when, for what quantity), then the goods are dispatched, then Sales issues the invoice. What moves is only WHO performs the dispatch: the act now belongs to the Store, the team that physically has the goods and prepares them, and the desk that sold them may no longer perform it. Everything the dispatch already did it still does - barcode/carton validation, the refusal of a quality-REJECTED carton (DEC-20260807-013), the cap at the quantity Quality approved, the single stock issue that reduces ERP stock, and the audit of who dispatched. Sales KEEPS its read of deliveries: it must still be able to see and trace what left against its orders, and reading is not dispatching. The permission consequence is deliberate and narrow: dispatch is gated on the STORE's own inventory permission, and the Store is NOT granted sales.manage or any wider Sales access to obtain it - the same two-sided shape Quality's dispatch sign-off already uses, where the record lives on a Sales model but the act is gated to the team that performs it. Expressly NOT decided here: whether Quality may withdraw an approval after goods have moved (still open from DEC-20260831-006), and whether the Store may also CANCEL or reverse a dispatch it made.
  - evidence: Owner instruction 01-Sep-2026, answering PENDING Q78 verbatim: 'the Store performs the final dispatch action. Sales does not perform dispatch.' plus the scope condition 'Keep Store preparation, recorded internal Quality approval, barcode validation, stock reduction, and audit. Give the Store only the permission needed for dispatch; do not grant wider Sales access.' Re-minted at integration: the id first assigned (DEC-20260901-001) was taken by an unrelated end-of-day-return decision on claude/store-inventory-e2e, and two different decisions may not share an id.
- **DEC-20260901-004** (2026-09-01, production, inventory) — MATERIAL SUBSTITUTION IS RECORDED AS TWO LINES, NEVER AS ONE EDITED LINE. When the floor cannot get all of a required material and an alternate is used in its place, the ORIGINAL line keeps the quantity of the original material that was ACTUALLY used, and the alternate material is added as a SEPARATE CONTROLLED LINE against the same requirement. The owner's worked example is the rule: required 6, original actually used 5, alternate used 1, total actual 6. The original line's actual quantity stays 5 and must never be written up to 6 - a single netted line of 6 would say the requirement was met by the original material, which is not what happened, and the whole reason to record a substitution is that it happened. WHAT THIS CHANGES, STATED ACCURATELY: until now the ERP REFUSED a substitution outright. StoreStoreIssueRequest rejected any issue line whose item differed from the item its material-request line asked for, with the message 'This line hands over a different material from the one the request asked for.' There was therefore NO way to record a substitution at all, and a floor that used an alternate either could not book the handover or had to book it against no requirement, losing the link to what was required. This decision opens that door, and opens it only under control. CONTROLLED means the substitute line must NAME WHAT IT STANDS IN FOR AND WHY: the item it substitutes for, and a reason, both recorded against the line. A line whose item differs from its requirement's item and which carries NO reason stays REFUSED exactly as it is today - the door opens for a recorded substitution and for nothing else, so a mis-picked line is still caught. The requirement's fulfilment counts BOTH lines: 5 of the original plus 1 of the alternate closes a requirement for 6, because the floor got what it needed. THREE THINGS ARE EXPRESSLY NOT DECIDED HERE. (1) WHICH items may substitute for which - there is no substitution master and none is created; any item that is otherwise issuable may be recorded as a substitute and the recorded reason is the only control, so nothing here validates a substitution against an engineering rule. (2) Whether a substitution needs an APPROVER above the person recording it - a reason and an actor are recorded, an approval workflow is not built, and if the factory wants a second signature that is a separate decision. (3) Whether RESIN substitution is permitted at all - resin is governed by FC-01 and the common-input rules, and nothing here is to be read as authorising a resin substitute.
  - evidence: Owner instruction 01-Sep-2026 (remaining ERP workflow work), verbatim: 'For material substitution: record the original actual quantity and add the alternate material as a separate controlled line. Example: required 6, original used 5, alternate used 1, total actual 6.' Prior-state evidence: StoreStoreIssueRequest::withValidator refuses a line whose item_id differs from its material request line's item_id. Re-minted at integration: the id first assigned (DEC-20260901-001) was taken by an unrelated decision on claude/store-inventory-e2e, and two different decisions may not share an id.
- **DEC-20260901-003** (2026-09-01, inventory, quality, production) — A DAMAGED RETURN NEVER GOES BACK TO USABLE STOCK. When unused raw material, packing material or a consumable comes back from Production, a GOOD return goes to the Store as usable stock exactly as before, and a DAMAGED return goes to QUALITY INSPECTION instead - it is never added to the Store's issuable balance on the way. Only after Quality has CONFIRMED the damage does the quantity move to Scrap. This resolves the narrowed PENDING Q89 and supersedes the recording-only boundary the return door shipped with, under which a damaged return moved exactly what a good one moved. HOW THE GUARANTEE IS MADE, because the mechanism is part of the rule: quality hold is an INTERNAL LOCATION of the one operational Store (DEC-20260830-002), a warehouse row exactly as Production/WIP is, so held material is out of the Store's issuable balance BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by a filter a later screen could forget - stock balances and every stock read are per item AND warehouse. Where no quality-hold location can be resolved the damaged return is REFUSED with a message naming the settings fix; it never falls back to the Store. No warehouse row is created by this decision: naming the location is a deliberate master-data act by a person. SCRAP IS AN ISSUE OUT OF STOCK, not a change of item identity - the same route incoming QC already uses for material it rejects (its Rejections Out issue) - because this ERP has no scrap-item mapping for a purchased input and DEC-20260901-002 expressly leaves which Scrap item undecided; nothing here invents or creates a Tally master. A damaged return still CLOSES its store issue's own quantity: the material did leave production, and the handover's arithmetic is about the floor, not about whether the material is usable. TWO THINGS ARE EXPRESSLY NOT DECIDED. (1) What Tally should receive when returned material is scrapped - the sibling clause DEC-20260825-001 already leaves open for QA rejection at arrival - and no voucher is posted or staged. (2) The RELEASE path, where Quality inspects and does NOT confirm damage, is built and is the agent's reading of the word 'directly' in 'a damaged return must never go directly back to usable stock': without it a mis-ticked line would strand good material permanently, which is the failure the return door exists to prevent. If that reading is wrong, say so and it is withdrawn.
  - evidence: Owner message 01-Sep-2026, verbatim: 'A good returned raw material, packing material, or consumable goes back to usable stock. A damaged return goes to Quality inspection. Only after Quality confirms the damage, move it to Scrap. A damaged return must never go directly back to usable stock.' Answers the narrowed Q89 recorded the same day. Implemented on branch claude/store-inventory-e2e.
- **DEC-20260901-002** (2026-09-01, production, quality, inventory) — DAMAGED FINISHED GOODS BECOME SCRAP. A finished good found damaged is not written off to nothing and is not returned to stock as a saleable finished good: it becomes Scrap, which this factory already treats as real stock booked inward per colour (FC-02, and 33 inward Scrap lines across the 38 real Stock Journals). This is a clarification the owner gave while narrowing Q89, and it settles the FINISHED GOOD half of 'what happens to damaged material' only. THREE THINGS ARE EXPRESSLY NOT DECIDED HERE. (1) The disposition of damaged RAW MATERIAL, PACKING MATERIAL or CONSUMABLES returned from Production stays OPEN as the narrowed Q89 - whether the Store may re-issue such material as it stands, whether it must wait for Quality, or whether it leaves stock as a write-off - and no agent may read this finished-goods answer across onto them. (2) Nothing here authorises building a finished-good-to-scrap conversion flow, a screen or a Tally posting; no such path exists today and creating one is a separate, deliberate piece of work. (3) Which Scrap item a given damaged finished good becomes is not decided here: ScrapItemResolver resolves scrap per colour for production output, and whether a damaged finished good follows the same mapping is unanswered - a scrap item name is a live Tally master and is never invented by an agent.
  - evidence: Owner message 01-Sep-2026, verbatim: 'Owner clarification for damage: damaged finished goods become Scrap.' Given in the same message that narrowed PENDING Q89 to damaged raw material, packing material and consumables and instructed that their disposition not be guessed. Consistent with FC-02 (scrap and lumps are real stock, booked inward).
- **DEC-20260901-001** (2026-09-01, inventory, production) — BOTH a partial and a full end-of-day return are allowed, and a FULL RETURN IS NOT MANDATORY. The Store may return part or all of the unused material at the end of the day, and material that is NOT returned remains in Production/WIP and carries forward as the next day's material on the floor. This CONFIRMS DEC-20260831-005 rather than changing it, and it is recorded rather than left implicit because a later owner instruction read as a mandatory end-of-day return: the two could not both be true, and an agent may not resolve that ambiguity by choosing. Concretely the ERP must NOT require Production/WIP to be empty at the end of a shift, must NOT refuse or flag a floor for being non-empty, and must keep netting the next material request against the usable quantity standing there (the three figures of DEC-20260831-005: total required, already available in Production/WIP, and the balance to request). This resolves PENDING Q88. NO CODE CHANGE FOLLOWS FROM IT - the shipped behaviour is already exactly this, which is why the answer is recorded as a confirmation and nothing was built or withdrawn to satisfy it.

- **DEC-20260831-012** (2026-08-31, sales, tally-sync, finance) — The ERP does NOT send Sales Orders, Delivery Notes or Sales Invoices to Tally. This REVERSES DEC-20260831-007, which had turned ERP-originated Delivery Note and Sales Invoice posting ON earlier the same day; the direction of the sales integration is now inbound only. TALLY ORIGINATES THE SALE on the accounting side: Tally creates the Sales Invoice and produces the e-invoice (IRN) and e-way-bill details, which the ERP never fabricates and never posts. The ERP's job is to IMPORT the Tally Sales Invoice XML, MATCH each imported voucher to the ERP Sales Order it belongs to, and UPDATE the ERP Sales Order's status from that match. The matching key is the CUSTOMER plus the CUSTOMER'S OWN PURCHASE-ORDER REFERENCE (sales_orders.customer_po_reference), which the ERP already records: in the factory's own 31-Aug export Tally's Sales voucher carries that string in BASICPURCHASEORDERNO / REFERENCE / ORDERNO and its Sales Order voucher carries the identical string in ORDERNO / REFERENCE, joining 32 of 55 Sales vouchers to a Sales Order with ZERO ambiguous keys. Voucher NUMBER is expressly NOT the key - Tally owns a contiguous NNN/26-27 series while the ERP mints INV-{id}, so the two numbering series never meet. This also resolves Q61 and Q72 (may the ERP emit a Tally Sales ORDER voucher) as NO. The ERP remains the origin of the FACTORY act - the sales order, the stock hold, the production request, the quality approval and the dispatch that reduces ERP stock are all the ERP's and are unaffected; only the accounting document direction is reversed. Expressly NOT decided here: whether the Store rather than Sales performs the final dispatch act (Q78 stays open), and what the ERP should do with an imported Tally invoice that matches NO ERP sales order (it is recorded as unmatched for a person to resolve, and is not permitted to create an order).
  - evidence: Owner instruction 31-Aug-2026 (Sales end-to-end build brief), requirement 7 verbatim: 'ERP must not send Sales Orders, Delivery Notes, or Sales Invoices to Tally. Tally creates the Sales Invoice, e-invoice, and e-way details. Import the Tally Sales Invoice XML, match it to the ERP Sales Order, and update the ERP status.' Matching-key evidence: Tally export read 31-Aug-2026 (~/Downloads/sales_voucher.xml, 55 Sales vouchers; ~/Downloads/test2_sales_order.xml, 34 Sales Order vouchers), fixtures extracted to backend/tests/Fixtures/tally/. Re-minted at integration: the id first assigned (DEC-20260831-008) was taken by an unrelated store-issue decision on another workflow branch, and two different decisions may not share an id.
- **DEC-20260831-011** (2026-08-31, quality) — Every arrival waits for incoming QA before the store may issue it. This required no new gate: a bag born on a goods receipt is already created waiting_qc, and DEC-20260825-001 already forbids held material leaving a store by any door. It had simply never fired, because no arrival ever created a bag. Making the lots block mandatory on weighed arrivals is what switches it on, so the two answers are one behaviour: receive, hold, inspect, release. Counted materials create no bags and so are not held — which follows from the limit recorded alongside the lot-capture decision, not from a separate ruling about QA.
  - evidence: Owner answer from Muthukumar Panchabekasan, 31-Aug-2026, to PENDING Q77 as posed ('Which materials must a goods receipt record lots and bags for?') and to the coupled QA clause of DEC-20260825-001, both asked with their options and answered in session. Answer given: 'Every arrival waits for QA'. This was already built and had never fired.
- **DEC-20260831-010** (2026-08-31, inventory) — A goods receipt must record what physically arrived — the lot and its bags — for every purchased material. IMPLEMENTED FOR WEIGHED MATERIALS ONLY, and the gap is not a choice: GoodsReceiptService refuses a lots block outright for any item not measured in kg, and the reconciliation beneath it is arithmetic in kilograms (a nominal or per-bag weight is mandatory, and bag_weight x bag_count must equal the received line quantity). Applied literally to a counted material the rule would REQUIRE a block the service REFUSES, so cartons, trays and film could not be received at all, and the only way to satisfy both rules would be to invent a kilogram weight for a carton and put a fiction into the stock ledger and into Tally. Weighed arrivals (resin, masterbatch) are therefore mandatory now; counted packaging is unchanged pending a unit-aware lot and an answer to what carries the barcode when one bag is a bundle of 500 cartons.
  - evidence: Owner answer from Muthukumar Panchabekasan, 31-Aug-2026, to PENDING Q77 as posed ('Which materials must a goods receipt record lots and bags for?') and to the coupled QA clause of DEC-20260825-001, both asked with their options and answered in session. Answer given: 'Every purchased material'. Recorded with the implementation limit that was found while applying it.
- **DEC-20260831-009** (2026-08-31, production) — A batch consumes from Production/WIP whenever that location holds a non-zero balance of the material, INCLUDING existing material that no Store Issue put there. FactoryWarehouseResolver::consumptionSource previously also required that a Store Issue had put the material there, so for the seven of nine live materials standing in production with no issue behind them the batch drew from the Store while the WIP kilograms sat untouched. Removing that condition does not open the over-consumption hole it guarded, because the surviving condition tests for a NON-ZERO balance rather than a positive one: an over-draw leaves Production/WIP negative, so it stays the source and the completion's shortfall record fires. What IS new: those materials now draw WIP to zero and then continue from the Store, and both movements carry purpose consumption differing only in warehouse_id, so the point at which the floor ran out is not marked in the ledger.

Implements the clause of DEC-20260831-005 that material not returned remains available in Production/WIP as the next day's opening material — until now honoured when netting the next request but not where a batch actually draws its material from.
- **DEC-20260831-008** (2026-08-31, inventory) — A Store Issue's claim on material lasts as long as returnable quantity remains on it, whatever its status: OPEN, PARTIALLY RETURNED and COMPLETED issues alike. Completing a Store Issue moves no stock, so a completed issue with quantity still outstanding is still holding material on the floor and its return must still name it. Anything keyed on StoreIssueStatus::isOpen (Issued|PartiallyReturned) treats a completed issue as finished and is wrong for this purpose — the UI gate on the handover return door was keyed that way and is now keyed on what is outstanding.

- **DEC-20260831-006** (2026-08-31, sales, quality) — Dispatch of finished goods is gated on INTERNAL QUALITY APPROVAL, and there is NO separate customer-approval step. The sequence is: stock is fully held against the sales order line, then Quality approves, then Sales dispatches, then Sales issues the invoice. Quality's approval must be RECORDED against the line — who approved, when, and for what quantity — not merely asserted, and a line may not be dispatched beyond the quantity Quality approved. This resolves Q27, which had left dispatch of not-yet-approved batches deliberately open since 07-Aug-2026 and is answered here as option (b), the QC pass required; it narrows DEC-20260807-013, under which a quality-REJECTED carton was refused at dispatch while a batch merely not yet through QC passed freely. Expressly settled: the customer-approval gate that earlier fulfilment work carried as an unbuilt 'not recorded' column does not exist and is to be removed rather than built, so no ERP screen, column or condition may imply a customer sign-off the factory does not perform. Expressly NOT decided here: whether the Store, rather than Sales, performs the final dispatch act (Q78 remains open) and whether Quality may withdraw an approval after goods have moved.
  - evidence: Owner message 31-Aug-2026: 'Internal Quality approval must be recorded and is required before dispatch. There is no separate customer approval step. The flow is: stock fully held -> Quality approves -> Sales dispatches -> Sales issues the invoice.' Re-minted at merge: the id first assigned was taken by an unrelated procurement decision already on main, and two different decisions may not share an id.
- **DEC-20260831-005** (2026-08-31, inventory, production) — At the end of production the storekeeper may return part or all of the unused material from Production/WIP to the Store; a partial return is as valid as a full one. If the material originally came through a Store Issue, the return MUST identify that exact Store Issue, so the handover's own quantity closes and the ledger records which handover the material came back on. Material standing in Production/WIP with NO Store Issue behind it may be returned without one — the rule reaches as far as a Store Issue exists to be named, and never requires inventing one. Material that is not returned REMAINS AVAILABLE in Production/WIP and is the next day's opening material on the floor; it is not consumed, not written off, and not moved by the passing of a day. When the next material request is prepared, the ERP MUST take account of the usable quantity already standing in Production/WIP for the SAME item and the SAME unit of measure, and the request screen must show three figures: the total material required, the quantity already available in Production/WIP, and the balance to request from the Store. The balance to request is the total required minus the usable quantity already in Production/WIP, floored at zero — a floor already covered on the production side means nothing is asked of the Store. Usable is narrower than present: a negative Production/WIP balance is a discrepancy and is netted as zero, and a quantity standing in a unit the item master no longer agrees with is reported but never subtracted (FC-03).
  - evidence: Owner decision and authorization given directly in session 31-Aug-2026, stated as five numbered points and prefaced 'Treat this as my factory-owner decision and authorization to implement, merge and deploy the complete flow.' Resolves PENDING Q69 (must the evening return name its Store Issue: yes, where one exists) and extends it with the WIP-aware net material request. Built on the return door deployed live as 05c86e1 (PR #52).
- **DEC-20260831-004** (2026-08-31, procurement) — When a purchase order is CANCELLED its quantity does NOT return to the purchase requisition's balance, provided the order had been sent. A requisition is asked for once and answered once: an order that reached the vendor has spent the requisition's allowance, and wanting that material again means raising a NEW requisition, which is a fresh approval by whoever approves them. The requisition, not the order, is the unit of authorisation. This answer needed a third one to be coherent, and it is part of the same decision: a cancelled order counts ONLY IF IT WAS EVER SENT. Because a draft reserves nothing, cancelling an unsent draft must release nothing — it was holding nothing — and without that qualification cancelling an abandoned draft would permanently consume a requisition the draft never held, so a typo could eat a requisition. The ERP records purchase_orders.sent_at to tell the two apart; rows already Sent, PartiallyReceived or Closed when the column was added are backfilled, and rows already Cancelled are left null and so read as never-sent, because the fact was not recorded and inventing one would decide a live requisition's balance on a guess.
  - evidence: Owner answer relayed in session 31-Aug-2026 to PENDING-OWNER-QUESTIONS 'When a purchase order is CANCELLED, does its quantity return to the requisition's balance?' — option B (cancelled still counts) chosen over the shipped default, plus the owner's narrowing answer that a PO cancelled while still an unsent draft must NOT consume the balance. Re-minted from DEC-20260831-002 at merge: that id was taken by an unrelated inventory decision already on main (the four stock figures), and two different decisions may not share an id.
- **DEC-20260831-003** (2026-08-31, procurement) — A purchase order holds quantity against its purchase requisition only once it has been SENT to the vendor. A DRAFT order reserves nothing: the requisition's Balance to Order is unchanged while a buyer is still typing, and a draft may be typed for any quantity. The consequence, accepted when this was decided: two drafts may each be raised for the whole requisition and the second is refused at Send, after the vendor and the rates have been typed, rather than at typing. The ERP therefore enforces the combined-quantity rule in PurchaseOrderService::send(), not at create or amend, and a guard on those paths would be unreachable rather than merely redundant.
  - evidence: Owner answer relayed in session 31-Aug-2026 to PENDING-OWNER-QUESTIONS 'Does a DRAFT purchase order already reserve quantity against its requisition?' — option B (draft does not reserve) chosen over the shipped default. Re-minted from DEC-20260831-001 at merge: that id was taken by an unrelated inventory decision already on main (the retired-warehouse movement-reference rule), and two different decisions may not share an id.
- **DEC-20260831-002** (2026-08-31, inventory) — The stock screen shows four figures per row: On hand, QA hold, Reserved, and Free to issue. 'Free to issue' is on hand less the incoming-QC hold and less outstanding customer reservations, clamped at zero. This is DELIBERATELY STRICTER than the engine: StockMovementService's outflow check subtracts the incoming-QC hold and does NOT subtract reservations, so the system will still permit issuing stock that is promised to a customer. The screen under-reports on purpose - a storekeeper who means to break a reservation may still do it, but must not do it by accident. The three component figures are shown beside the headline so nothing is hidden and the difference from the engine is visible rather than silent. This resolves PENDING Q79. It changes no stock arithmetic and no write path; it is a reading of existing figures. Expressly NOT decided here: whether the ENGINE should also refuse an issue that breaks a reservation - that remains as it is, and changing it would be a separate decision about what the factory permits, not about what a screen says.
  - evidence: Owner instruction from Muthukumar Panchabekasan, 31-Aug-2026, answering PENDING Q79 ('What should the stock screen call the quantity a storekeeper may act on?'): 'ship the four columns', accepting the proposed shape On hand / QC hold / Reserved / Free to issue with Free to issue subtracting BOTH the QC hold and customer reservations.

Raw material, packing material, work in progress and finished goods all belong to that single operational Store; they are distinguished by inventory CATEGORY, STOCK STATE or INTERNAL LOCATION, never by separate physical Tally godowns. This supersedes DEC-20260817-001's reading of 'Raw Material Store -> Production/WIP -> Finished Goods Store' as three separate places. It expressly does NOT supersede the invariant that decision protects, which stands unchanged: 'issued to production but not yet consumed' remains a real stock state, distinct from both store stock and from consumption, and it is carried by the Production/WIP INTERNAL LOCATION - the warehouse row coded WIP - which must remain resolvable by the application whether or not any picker offers it. Folding that row's balances into the Store would destroy the only state separating the floor from the store and is NOT authorised by this decision. - **DEC-20260825-003** (2026-08-25, procurement, erp-surface, tally-sync) — Vendor is a CONFIGURATION master, and a purchase order selects a vendor from that configuration rather than inventing one. Three parts. (1) The vendor master lives on the Configuration Lifecycle Contract already in force for the other masters (DEC-20260817-002, which this does not replace): create, view, edit, activate/deactivate, archive, and hard delete only where the record is proven never-used and dependency-free. (2) A purchase order offers the ACTIVE configured vendors. Where the vendor a buyer needs is absent, an authorized user creates it in Configuration and then raises the order; the creation happens on the vendor master screen, not inline on the purchase order, so a vendor is never created as a side effect of getting an order out. (3) A vendor MAY be saved without an exact Tally ledger mapping, because the master must not be blocked waiting on Accounts - but a vendor whose Tally ledger is unmapped has its Tally Purchase Order posting WITHHELD and REFUSED, never posted against a guessed or approximately-matched ledger. That refusal is the rule DEC-20260812-002 already states for a vendor with no Tally identity; this decision re-affirms it for the configuration path and does not supersede or weaken it. One thing is expressly NOT decided here and remains open: PENDING Q53(c), whether a RETIRED vendor should also block a Tally-MIRROR purchase order (source: tally), stays unanswered, and the narrow behaviour pinned by the existing mirror test is unchanged by this decision.

Boundaries: Sync Now never pulls masters or stock FROM Tally, and it never posts, delivers or acknowledges a voucher from the browser - only the local agent posts to Tally, and only vouchers already queued are affected. Only an Owner/Accounts permission may press it. If the agent is offline the request simply waits until the agent next polls; nothing is lost, and the ERP never claims a voucher posted that has not. Duplicate or concurrent clicks must not create a duplicate queue entry or a duplicate Tally voucher - a repeat click is a no-op on the queue, while every press is recorded. The factory tray's own "Sync Vouchers Now" stays exactly as it is.

- **DEC-20260825-001** (2026-08-25, inventory, production, tally-sync) — Material that has bags standing in incoming-QC hold (waiting_qc) may not leave a store's stock balance through any outflow door: not a Store Issue, not a generic stock issue, not a stock transfer, not a production completion's material consumption, and not a Tally stock reconciliation. The single exception is QA's rejection at incoming inspection, which may remove the quantity that inspection has actually rejected, and nothing more - no other actor and no other route may remove held material. QA's ACCEPTANCE is not a removal: accepted bags simply leave the hold and become issuable like any other stock. This is a hold on ISSUANCE only - it does not defer, condition or otherwise change GRN stock posting. The hold reaches only material that actually HAS bags in waiting_qc; this decision creates no hold for material that has none. Three things are expressly NOT decided here and remain open: what carries the barcode for counted packaging, what Tally should receive when material is rejected at QA (an accepted-only Receipt Note, or a full Receipt Note plus a separate rejection voucher), and whether every arrival line must wait for QA before the store may issue it or only named materials.
  - evidence: Owner confirmation 25-Aug-2026, approving verbatim: 'Material with bags in waiting_qc cannot leave through Store Issue, generic issue, transfer, production completion, or Tally reconciliation. Only QA rejection may remove the rejected quantity.' The implementation this approves is PR #24 (decisionm/production-erp, branch codex/inward-qc-hold) at commit bf1b2fa0ce494e3afeb825323ec219f4cb6971fc, which is UNMERGED and undeployed at the time of recording.

- **DEC-20260817-002** (2026-08-17, erp-surface, inventory, production) — Configuration masters carry a real hard delete, but only for records proven never-used and dependency-free; everything else is Archive. Five rules govern it. (1) Hard delete is permitted only where the record has never been used and nothing depends on it. (2) An ARCHIVED record retains and reserves its business code: historical codes are never reused, so a retired code stays taken. A genuinely unused record that is hard-deleted may release its code, because nothing in history ever referred to it. (3) Hard delete is Super Admin / Owner level only; other permitted configuration users may create, edit, activate and deactivate according to RBAC. (4) Archiving or deactivating in the ERP causes NO automatic Tally mutation: historical Tally identity and mapping are preserved, and any change to a Tally master is a separate, explicit action. (5) 'Ever used' means historical references, maintenance schedules and every other dependency, not merely current foreign keys; audit evidence is built or preserved where needed, and where historical use cannot be safely proven for legacy data the system REFUSES the hard delete and offers Archive only. Destructive cascade must never be used to make a dependency check pass.
  - evidence: Lead's answer to Q52, 17-Aug-2026 session ('Hard delete is required, but only for configuration records proven never-used and dependency-free ... If historical use cannot be proven safely for legacy data, refuse hard delete and allow Archive only'); the audited baseline it answers is docs/engineering/AUDIT-CONFIGURATION-LIFECYCLE-2026-08-17.md
- **DEC-20260812-003** (2026-08-12, procurement, compliance, tally-sync) — Purchase and tax settings are CONFIGURATION, not code: GST rates come from the government and change, so once set they are held as data a person maintains, the way production already has a configuration. Three parts. (1) The company's own state decides local versus interstate — proven by the 12-Aug Day Book, where 90 of 92 vouchers follow Local ledger with a Puducherry party and CGST+SGST, Interstate with any other state and IGST. (2) The purchase ledger is chosen per (local or interstate) x rate, because Tally actually uses FOUR purchase ledgers and a single Purchase mapping cannot express that. (3) GST RATES MUST BE EFFECTIVE-DATED, and this is the load-bearing part: the owner's own export proves the same items were booked at 5 percent and at 18 percent in different months, so one rate per item or per HSN would misprice either the history or the present. A rate is held as 'this rate, from this date', the same shape as a superseding decision record — a new rate never edits the old one, and a voucher dated in April resolves to April's rate. Vendor payment terms and delivery defaults belong to the vendor they describe, not to a global setting, because the data shows them varying per vendor (45 days on 51 of 92 orders, 60 on 17, also 30 and 15). NO TAX RATE IS EVER SEEDED AS A DEFAULT. Leave days were seeded as a starting point because a wrong leave figure is corrected on review; a wrong tax rate is money. The container is built and left empty, and the accountant — who is accountable for it — decides which item is which rate. That question is open and explicitly not the agent's: published Indian GST rates put paper and cardboard packaging at 5 percent since 22-Sep-2025 while plastic packaging stays 18 percent, which would make the split appear in every month, yet the data shows 5 percent only in April, May and June, and the owner understands the recent change as everything now being 18 percent. Those readings disagree, so the configuration must be able to hold BOTH rates and the accountant resolves which applies.
  - evidence: Owner instruction relayed in session 12-Aug-2026 ('the way production has a configuration, this needs a configuration'); measured from the 12-Aug Tally Day Book export (manifest tally-daybook-po-20260812, -part2): four purchase ledgers, 90 of 92 conforming to the Puducherry local/interstate rule, and 9 of 43 items appearing at BOTH 5% and 18% in different months
- **DEC-20260812-002** (2026-08-12, procurement, tally-sync) — Purchase orders are raised in the ERP from now on, not in Tally, and the ERP sends each one to Tally as a Purchase Order voucher. One book of purchase orders, not two. This completes the direction already true for goods receipts: the ERP raises, Tally records. The consequence, stated plainly: the accountant stops keying purchase orders into Tally, and a purchase order keyed directly into Tally after the cutover would be invisible to the ERP's remaining-quantity tracking, so the two books would stop agreeing. The build that follows must post a Tally Purchase Order voucher through an enqueuePurchaseOrder() path shaped like the existing Receipt Note path — vendor resolved to its Tally ledger, items to their Tally stock items, nothing hardcoded. It is an ORDER voucher and must not touch accounts or stock in Tally; that is to be stated in the code and proved by a test. Where a vendor or an item has no Tally identity the ERP refuses to post rather than guessing, surfaced the way unmapped names are surfaced today. The existing PurchaseOrder columns are used honestly: source records where the order was raised, tally_order_no records what Tally accepted it as, and neither is invented. Nothing changes on the day this is recorded; the build comes after the owner's meeting and the goods-receipt fix. Five questions are deliberately left open for the owner and the accountant rather than assumed: the cutover date, whether open orders already in Tally finish there or move to the ERP, whose purchase-order NUMBER is authoritative, whether the accountant wants an order voucher in Tally at all, and whether a Tally Purchase Order voucher needs the Purchase ledger mapped or only the vendor ledger.
  - evidence: Owner instruction relayed in session 12-Aug-2026 ('THE PURCHASE ORDER IS RAISED IN THE ERP FROM NOW ON ... One book, not two'); docs/PURCHASE-RESIN-BARCODE-AUDIT.md records the pre-change state where the PO screen's 'Mirrored from Tally' switch treats Tally as the source of truth
- **DEC-20260812-001** (2026-08-12, erp-surface, hrms, payroll) — HRMS and Payroll are adopted and visible in the ERP; CRM and Finance stay hidden. This keeps the adoption principle of DEC-20260809-001 — the ERP surfaces only modules the factory has adopted, adoption is a one-line source edit in ADOPTED_MODULES, and nothing is ever deleted or disabled — and changes only which modules are in that list. The grounds for un-hiding HRMS are that hiding it never protected anything: Employee is what shift_production_entries.operator_id, supervisor_signed_by and ShiftSummary.supervisor point at, so the Start Batch operator dropdown has been offering the seven demo people (EMP-001..EMP-007) to the floor all along. Those seven rows are therefore KEPT, NOT DELETED: the factory edits them into real people on the Employees screen, which fixes the operator dropdown at the same time and preserves every existing link from real production records. A demo NAME is a label the factory overwrites; a demo POSTING is a false record, so demo transactions against those people (attendance, leave requests, payroll runs, payslips) are listed for the owner and cleared only on his word, separately. Leave types, salary components, a simple monthly salary structure and current-year leave balances are seeded on the owner's instruction using ordinary Indian factory standards (Casual Leave 12 days, Sick Leave 12, Earned/Privilege Leave 15; Basic, HRA and allowances with PF and ESI as deductions) as a STARTING POINT ONLY — every seeded row must be visibly marked as a default the factory has not yet confirmed, in the same spirit as the downtime reasons' To Confirm marker, because a number nobody has agreed to must never look like a number somebody agreed to. The factory's real policy replaces these; the open questions (which leave types are actually given, days per year for each, carry-forward, monthly versus daily-wage versus piece-rate, OT rate, PF/ESI applicability, payroll period and payday, and whether payroll should ever post to Tally) are recorded as pending, not answered by the defaults. CRM stays hidden until the factory records its first real enquiry, since opening three empty screens is the complaint the adoption rule exists to prevent.
  - evidence: Owner instruction relayed in session 12-Aug-2026 ('RENAME, DO NOT DELETE ... unhide hrms AND payroll ... seed a standard policy, labelled as a starting point'); live read 12-Aug-2026 confirming all seven demo employees present on erpdemo.amrtech.in

Hand-written or hand-edited records are unsupported: every record must byte-match the canonical tool serialization (pinned JSON parameters), and validation fails any file that does not. The owner's human surface is CURRENT-DECISIONS.md; raw records are machine format (FC-08).
